history.alt_text: A split-screen comparison of a brand-new asphalt roof shingle and a severely weathered, cracked shingle resting on a concrete floor.
history.caption: Class 4 impact ratings test fresh shingles, but real-world weathering makes panels significantly more vulnerable to hail.
history.title: shingle-weathering-class4-comparison

style_when: the story is a product, a device, a price or a market for a thing the reader could buy — an appliance, a panel, a router, a robot arm
prompt: split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast. Studio product photograph of a heavy asphalt roof shingle resting on a weathered concrete floor in a garage. The left half shows a pristine, brand-new charcoal shingle with perfect tactile granule texture; the right half shows a heavily weathered, slate grey shingle with exposed fiberglass, micro-cracks, and stripped granules. 85mm lens, shallow depth of field, fine film grain. A single directional key light from the left casts a long, distinct shadow across the concrete. Palette of bone white, slate grey, and charcoal. Catalogue clarity, no text, no printed lettering.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, people, hands, plain studio background, empty gradient void
rationale: A studio object approach applied as a split-screen allows a highly controlled, tactile comparison between a fresh roofing product (what the label tests) and an aged product (the real-world reality), focusing on the material degradation.
subject: a pristine asphalt shingle contrasted with a heavily weathered shingle
core_thesis: The Class 4 impact rating evaluates only pristine new shingles, obscuring the severe vulnerability of aged, weather-worn roofing to hail damage.
core_conflict: Fresh lab-tested resilience vs. real-world weathered material degradation.
composition: split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast

review.depicts: A split-screen image showing a new, intact piece of roofing material on the left and a damaged, weathered piece of roofing material on the right, both resting on a cracked concrete surface.
review.reason: The image directly illustrates the article's focus on comparing new versus aged and damaged roofing shingles.
